slides.title: Introduction & Background
slides.task_brief:
Slide title: 'Introduction & Background'. Body bullets (22pt, max 6):

- Telegram is the dominant messaging platform for Ethiopian university students, with millions of daily active users.
- Informal job channels (Afriwork, Yegna Tutors Harrar) post tutoring, freelance, and part-time roles daily.
- These channels are free, instant, and reach a large targeted audience.
- However, posts are unstructured free text with no filtering, no archive, and no verification.
- Temariware proposes a structured Telegram Mini App + Bot to solve these gaps.
- Combines the reach of Telegram with the structure of a traditional job-matching platform.

Speaker notes: 3-5 bullet hints on why this background motivates the project.

slides.title: Statement of the Problem
slides.task_brief:
Slide title: 'Statement of the Problem'. Body bullets (22pt, max 6):

- Job posts are unstructured free text — impossible to filter by subject, location, or salary.
- No persistent archive — opportunities disappear from chat history within hours.
- Neither employers nor students are verified — scams and no-shows are common.
- Application process is highly manual — students forward CVs repeatedly, no tracking.
- No payment mechanism — channels cannot sustain themselves or filter serious applicants.
- Existing platforms (EthioJobs, Ezega) focus on full-time graduate roles, not student part-time work.

Speaker notes: brief hints on each pain point with a real example.

slides.title: General Objective
slides.task_brief:
Slide title: 'General Objective'. Centered key message in a callout block (large, 24pt):

'To design, develop, and deploy a Telegram Mini App and Bot called Temariware that connects Ethiopian university students with verified tutoring, freelance, part-time, and full-time job opportunities, while providing integrated payment verification, mandatory document checks, and automated hiring workflow management.'

Below the callout, three small stat blocks showing the scope:
- 3 user roles (Student, Employer, Admin)
- 3 languages (EN, Amharic, Afaan Oromoo)
- 0 ETB monthly cost (free-tier infrastructure)

Speaker notes: hints on emphasising the integration of payment + verification + workflow.

slides.title: Specific Objectives
slides.task_brief:
Slide title: 'Specific Objectives'. Two-column layout with 10 numbered objectives across two columns (5 left, 5 right):

Left column (1-5):
1. Analyse limitations of existing informal Telegram job channels and elicit stakeholder requirements.
2. Design a multi-section Mini App UI (job feed, detail, post, applications, profile, admin) with 3-language support.
3. Design and implement a PostgreSQL database schema via Prisma ORM (users, jobs, applications, payments, subscriptions, verifications, settings).
4. Implement a Telegram Bot webhook handling 9 slash commands and pushing instant alerts.
5. Implement Telegram WebApp initData HMAC-SHA256 authentication.

Right column (6-10):
6. Implement screenshot-based payment verification (job post fee + per-job application fee).
7. Implement mandatory document upload (National ID, University ID, grade report) with image compression.
8. Implement automatic job closure when positionsAvailable is reached.
9. Deploy on free-tier infrastructure (Vercel + Neon Postgres + Telegram Bot API).
10. Document the system per the Dire Dawa University industrial project guideline.

Speaker notes: brief hints on which objectives were completed vs in-progress.

slides.title: Scope of the Project
slides.task_brief:
Slide title: 'Scope of the Project'. Two-column layout with 'In Scope' (left) and 'Out of Scope' (right) headers:

Left column — In Scope:
- Next.js Mini App with 6 primary views
- Telegram bot with 9 slash commands
- PostgreSQL database with 7 entities
- HMAC-based authentication layer
- Screenshot-based payment verification
- Mandatory document upload with compression
- Per-job configurable application fees
- Automatic job closure on hiring target
- Channel broadcast to @TEMARIWARE
- Per-subscriber push alerts

Right column — Out of Scope (v2):
- Real Chapa / Telebirr API integration
- Automated scraping of existing channels
- In-app CV file storage (uses external links)
- Email or SMS notifications
- Employer dashboard with multi-job analytics
- Saved/bookmarked jobs
- Reporting beyond basic admin stats

Speaker notes: hints on why each out-of-scope item was deferred.

slides.title: Limitations
slides.task_brief:
Slide title: 'Limitations'. Body bullets (22pt, max 6):

- Payment verification is manual (screenshot review) — introduces hours of latency, single point of failure.
- System depends entirely on Telegram — no Telegram account, no access; outages affect availability.
- Images stored as base64 in PostgreSQL (not object storage) — 1MB practical limit per image.
- No automated authenticity checks on uploaded IDs — relies on admin visual inspection.
- Currently supports only the Ethiopian market and three languages.
- No in-app dispute resolution mechanism — handled via external Telegram chat.

Speaker notes: brief hints on mitigation strategies for each limitation.

slides.title: Methodology & Approach
slides.task_brief:
Slide title: 'Methodology & Approach'. Body bullets (22pt, max 6):

- Object-Oriented Software Development approach (per university guideline).
- Iterative and incremental development process — each iteration produces a working slice.
- Loosely based on the Agile Unified Process — lightweight upfront design + continuous integration.
- Five phases: Requirements, Design, Implementation, Testing, Deployment.
- Each phase ends with advisor review milestone for continuous feedback.
- Continuous deployment to Vercel staging environment throughout development.

Speaker notes: hints on how the iterative approach handled changing requirements.

slides.title: Significance of the Project
slides.task_brief:
Slide title: 'Significance of the Project'. Body bullets (22pt, max 6) covering three stakeholder groups:

- For Students: reduces friction of finding part-time work; subscribe to subject/location alerts; apply with one tap using pre-verified profile; mandatory documents build trust with employers.
- For Employers: structured applicant tracking; per-job application fee filters casual browsers; review documents in one panel; accept/reject with one tap; auto-close positions when hiring target met.
- For the Ecosystem: reference implementation of a production Telegram Mini App on free-tier infrastructure; demonstrates youth entrepreneurship without upfront capital; formalises a previously informal labour market.
- Creates data on youth employment patterns for future research.
- Sustainable revenue model through configurable fees.
- Multilingual (EN/AM/OR) ensures accessibility across Ethiopia.

Speaker notes: hints on which significance point resonates most with the committee.

slides.title: Current System Description
slides.task_brief:
Slide title: 'Current System Description'. Body bullets (22pt, max 6):

- Informal Telegram channels (Afriwork, Yegna Tutors Harrar) broadcast job posts as free text.
- Employer composes a free-text message and forwards to channel operator's bot.
- Operator manually reviews, reformats, and publishes to the channel.
- Interested students forward the post + CV to employer's personal Telegram.
- Employer reviews applications in private chat, contacts candidates directly.
- Payments (when required) made via Telebirr with no formal record.

Speaker notes: brief hints on a real example from each channel.

slides.task_brief:

Left column (FR-01 to FR-05):

slides.title: Non-Functional Requirements
slides.task_brief:
Slide title: 'Non-Functional Requirements'. Render a table (class 'tbl') with 7 rows. Columns: ID | Category | Requirement. Body rows:

- NFR-01 | Performance | API response < 500ms (95th percentile); Mini App first paint < 2s on 3G

Speaker notes: brief hints on how each NFR was tested.

slides.title: Business Rules & Constraints
slides.task_brief:
Slide title: 'Business Rules & Constraints'. Two-column layout:

Left column — Key Business Rules:
- Only verified employers or admins can post jobs.
- Students cannot apply until profile is complete (3 documents uploaded).
- One application per student per job (unique constraint).
- Job posting requires payment screenshot (default 500 ETB).
- Application fees are per-job configurable by employer.
- Auto-close when filledPositions reaches positionsAvailable.

Right column — Key Constraints:
- Free-tier infrastructure only (zero recurring cost).
- Screenshot-based payment (no Chapa API in v1).
- Images stored as base64 in PostgreSQL (1MB max).
- Mini App runs inside Telegram WebApp container.
- No web_app buttons in channel posts (only URL buttons).
- Three languages with runtime switching.

Speaker notes: brief hints on which constraint shaped the design most.

slides.title: Essential Use Case Model
slides.task_brief:
Slide title: 'Essential Use Case Model'. Body: 'Four primary actors, fifteen use cases' as a sub-heading. Two-column layout listing use cases by actor:

Left column — Student & Employer:
- Student: Browse Job Feed, View Job Detail, Complete Profile, Apply to Job, Subscribe to Alerts, Upload Payment, View My Applications
- Employer: Post Job, Review Applicants, Accept Applicant, Reject Applicant, Verify Employer

Right column — Administrator & Bot:
- Administrator: Approve Job, Approve Payment, Approve Verification, Configure Settings
- Telegram Bot: Handle Slash Commands, Push Job Alerts, Broadcast to Channel

Below: callout block — 'Include relationship: Apply to Job includes Check Profile Complete. Extend relationship: Post Job extends Upload Payment Screenshot (only when fee > 0). Full use case diagram in Chapter 2, Figure 2.7.'

Speaker notes: brief hints on the most important use case path.

slides.title: Conceptual Class Model
slides.task_brief:
Slide title: 'Conceptual Class Model'. Body bullets (22pt, max 6):

- Seven primary classes: User, Job, Application, Subscription, VerificationRequest, Setting, Payment.
- A User has many Jobs (as employer), many Applications (as student), many Subscriptions, and may have one VerificationRequest.
- A Job has many Applications and may have associated Payments.
- An Application belongs to one User and one Job, with a unique constraint on (jobId, userId).
- A Setting is a singleton (single row) storing global configuration.
- Payment is an audit log linking a User, Job, and optionally an Application.

Below: callout — 'Full class diagram with attributes and operations in Chapter 3, Figure 3.5. Complete Prisma schema in Appendix C.'

Speaker notes: brief hints on why a singleton Setting was chosen.

slides.title: Sequence & Activity Diagrams
slides.task_brief:
Slide title: 'Sequence & Activity Diagrams'. Two-column layout:

Left column — Sequence Diagrams:
- Apply to Job: Mini App → Jobs API → Applications API → Database → Employer (Telegram notification)
- Accept Applicant and Pay: Employer → Accept API → Student (notification) → Pay API → Admin → Approve Payment API
- Approve Job and Broadcast: Admin → Approve API → Channel (Telegram Bot API) → Subscribers (push)

Right column — Activity Diagrams:
- Job Posting & Approval Flow: submit → payment screenshot → admin review → approve/reject → broadcast → alerts
- Application Lifecycle: PENDING → ACCEPTED → PAYMENT_PENDING → HIRED (or REJECTED/CLOSED)
- Auto-close trigger: when filledPositions = positionsAvailable, mark job CLOSED, notify all parties

Below: callout — 'Full diagrams in Chapter 2, Figures 2.9–2.13.'

Speaker notes: brief hints on which flow was hardest to design.

slides.title: Software Architecture
slides.task_brief:
Slide title: 'Software Architecture'. Body bullets (22pt, max 6):

- Selected style: Layered Architecture with four layers — Presentation, Application, Domain, Persistence.
- Presentation Layer: React 19 components (Mini App views).
- Application Layer: Next.js API routes (controllers).
- Domain Layer: Prisma models + business logic.
- Persistence Layer: PostgreSQL on Neon (Frankfurt, eu-central-1).
- Chosen for clear separation of concerns, Next.js convention alignment, team familiarity.

Below: callout — 'Alternatives considered: Microkernel (too complex), Event-Driven (unnecessary complexity), Serverless-First (already adopted at deployment). Full comparison in Chapter 3, Table 3.1.'

Speaker notes: brief hints on why layered was chosen over microservices.

slides.title: Component & Deployment
slides.task_brief:
Slide title: 'Component & Deployment'. Two-column layout:

Left column — Components:
- Next.js Mini App (Vercel) — frontend + API routes
- Telegram Bot Webhook (within Next.js) — receives updates
- PostgreSQL Database (Neon Frankfurt) — data persistence
- Telegram Bot API (external) — message sending + initData
- @TEMARIWARE Channel (external) — public job broadcast

Right column — Deployment Nodes:
- Vercel Edge Network — runs Next.js globally
- Neon Cloud (Frankfurt) — PostgreSQL, closest to Ethiopia
- Telegram Cloud — Bot API + channel hosting
- End users access via Telegram client (mobile/desktop/web)
- Webhook: Telegram Cloud → Vercel via HTTPS

Below: callout — 'Full diagrams in Chapter 3, Figures 3.2 and 3.3.'

Speaker notes: brief hints on why Frankfurt region was chosen.

slides.title: Conclusion & Future Work
slides.task_brief:
Slide title: 'Conclusion & Future Work'. Two-column layout:

Left column — Conclusion:
- Temariware successfully addresses the structural gaps in Ethiopia's informal Telegram job market.
- All 10 specific objectives were achieved.
- System is deployed, live, and accepting real users on free-tier infrastructure.
- Combines structured job matching, document verification, and payment workflow in one platform.
- Demonstrates that production-grade software can be built with zero recurring cost in Ethiopia.

Right column — Future Work (v2):
- Integrate Chapa / Telebirr API for automated payment verification.
- Migrate image storage to Supabase Storage or AWS S3.
- Add in-app messaging between students and employers.
- Automated scraping and import from existing Telegram channels.
- Add employer dashboard with multi-job analytics.
- Add saved/bookmarked jobs with daily digest.
- Expand to other East African markets.

Speaker notes: brief hints on what you'd improve first.
